newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - July 3.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - July 3.

text.p: Following are views on the direction of Philippine stocks on Thursday and main factors likely to affect trading:

* Market will continue to experience selling pressure as fund managers in Hong Kong return from a three-day holiday although this may be muted by the Central Bank's strong defense of the peso, BPI Securities Corp analyst Spencer Yap said. The Bank rushed to defend the peso on Wednesday after Thailand said it was allowing a managed float of its currency.
* Sun Hung Kai Securities expects the market to test a 2,750 support level. Others see the support lower at 2,600 points.
* On Wednesday, the Philippine composite index closed 50.65 points lower at 2,764.89 points as wild swings in the foreign exchange market scared stock market investors.
* The Dow Jones on Wednesday ended 73.05 points up at 7,795.38 PLDT's ADR closed down $0/at $64 1/8.

* The Philippine peso closed at 26.376 after reaching a low of 26.380, recovering lost ground after the Central Bank flooded the market with millions of dollars and raised its rate to quell a speculative attack after the Thai baht tumble.
* The Philippine interbank call loan average was up at 15.09375 pct vs 15.0625 pct.

* The Central Bank said on Thursday it had set its overnight lending rate at 26 percent from a previous 17 percent. The adjustment in the rate came after the Central Bank raised its overnight borrowing rate by nine percentage points to 24 percent on Wednesday.
* The Philippines could still be forced into a drawn-out war to defend its currency after speculators pressured Thailand to change its exchange rate policy to a managed float, bankers told Reuters.
* Thailand's de facto devaluation sent tremors through the region on Wednesday and analysts warned that even if neighboring economies were in better shape there was a risk of infection.
* Manila banks stayed away from the secondary T-bill market after the Central Bank's two successive increases in its key rate.

* The Philippines is determined to defend its peso from speculative attack but the latest spillover from the effective devaluation of the Thai baht should die down, Central Bank Governor Gabriel Singson told Reuters.
* The Securities and Exchange Commission has approved the transformation of oil exploration firm Unioil & Gas Development Co Inc into a holding firm.

* Inquirer reported that President Fidel Ramos said a mission from the International Monetary Fund believed the Philippine economy was sound but lacked some legislative changes. Congress is yet to pass a comprehensive tax reform package considered a pre-condition for the Philippines to exit from IMF tutelage.
